summary:
**AEROKRYPT** is a planetary analogue research and discovery platform developed to help researchers explore terrestrial locations that may offer useful comparisons for studying Mars and the Moon. It brings location discovery, site evaluation, and scientific information together in one interactive platform.

Users can explore curated Earth analogue sites, examine their geological characteristics, view available imagery and map-based information, and compare relevant environmental features with planetary research objectives. The platform also highlights available evidence and data gaps, helping users understand both the potential relevance and limitations of each location.

AEROKRYPT addresses the challenge of making planetary analogue research more accessible, organized, and evidence-driven. By bringing relevant information from scientific sources and exploration datasets into a unified interface, it supports more informed site exploration and preliminary research assessment.

This is important because studying suitable Earth analogues can help researchers investigate planetary environments and prepare for future exploration, while encouraging transparent, data-supported scientific interpretation.
details:
Project Details — AEROKRYPT

AEROKRYPT is an interactive planetary analogue research platform designed to help users discover and evaluate Earth locations that may be relevant to studying the geological and environmental conditions of Mars and the Moon.

How It Works

The platform brings together four main sections:

  • Location Explore: Allows users to discover curated terrestrial analogue locations and explore their geological characteristics through interactive maps and a 3D Earth globe.
  • Site Evaluation: Helps users examine and compare Earth locations with Mars and Moon research environments using available geological, terrain, imagery, and environmental information. It also highlights missing data and limitations.
  • Research Hub: Provides a space for organizing research, entering information, saving results, and creating evaluations.
  • Public Discovery: Makes planetary exploration knowledge more accessible through scientific instruments and technology references, learning resources, case studies, and published research.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AEROKRYPT organizes relevant planetary analogue information in one accessible platform. It can help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts explore potential analogue environments, understand geological similarities and differences, and identify areas requiring further investigation.

Its intended impact is to support more informed preliminary research, improve access to planetary science information, and encourage interest in planetary exploration.

Tools and Technologies

The project uses modern web development and geospatial technologies, including:

  • Frontend: React.js, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Vite.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Database: PostgreSQL and PostGIS for structured and geospatial information.
  • Mapping and Visualization: Leaflet, Three.js, react-globe.gl, and Recharts.
  • Scientific Data Sources and Standards: NASA planetary datasets, USGS resources, ESA resources, and STAC-based data discovery.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Antigravity IDE, Git, and GitHub.

Creativity and Innovation

AEROKRYPT combines interactive Earth exploration, planetary comparison, scientific information, and research organization in a single platform. Its use of a 3D globe alongside map-based exploration gives users a more engaging way to discover potential analogue locations.

An important design principle is scientific transparency. The platform distinguishes between measured, sourced, estimated, and unavailable information rather than presenting missing information as established fact. It also treats analogue relevance as a research possibility, not proof that an Earth location is identical to a Martian or lunar environment.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered scientific accuracy, reliability of data sources, accessibility, usability, visual clarity, geospatial information, and the limitations of available datasets. The platform was designed to make complex planetary research information easier to explore while avoiding unsupported scientific conclusions.
